questions.stem: What does local anaesthetic fill in a Bier block?
questions.answer: The venous system of a limb emptied by gravity or compression and cut off from the circulation by a tourniquet

questions.stem: In a Bier block, how soon does indirect anaesthesia develop distal to the distal cuff?
For what type of surgery is a Bier block suited?
questions.answer: Short surgery or manipulation of the upper or lower limb

questions.stem: In a Bier block, for which limb is the technique most accepted?
Which typical short upper limb procedures suit a Bier block?
questions.answer: Radial fracture reduction and carpal tunnel release

questions.stem: For foot, ankle or distal leg surgery, what is the longest duration suited to a Bier block?
For which condition is a Bier block an alternative to repeated sympathetic ganglion blocks?
questions.answer: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS)

questions.stem: How long can chemical sympathectomy from a Bier block with guanethidine last?
Which limb injury is a contraindication to Bier block?
Which skin condition at the site is a contraindication to Bier block?
Which vascular problem in the limb contraindicates a Bier block?
questions.answer: Severe vascular injury of the limb

questions.stem: Which existing vascular feature contraindicates a Bier block?
questions.answer: Existing arteriovenous shunt

questions.stem: Why is a Bier block unsuitable for surgery expected to last over 1 hour?
questions.answer: Tourniquet pain

questions.stem: Where should the cannula be placed for an upper limb Bier block?
questions.answer: In a peripheral vein as distal as possible

questions.stem: Where is the double pneumatic tourniquet placed in an upper limb Bier block?
Besides elevation, how is the upper limb exsanguinated in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Esmarch bandage wrapped from fingertips to the distal cuff

questions.stem: How much is the proximal cuff inflated in an upper limb Bier block?
What volume of 0.5% lidocaine is used for an upper limb Bier block?
What is the maximum lidocaine concentration for a Bier block?
How quickly does 0.5% lidocaine take effect in an upper limb Bier block?
In an upper limb Bier block, when is the distal cuff inflated and the proximal cuff deflated?
questions.answer: After about 25–30 minutes of anaesthesia, or with tourniquet pain

questions.stem: What is the minimum cuff time in a Bier block, even for a very short procedure?
Which local anaesthetic is preferred in Europe for a Bier block?
Does alkalinising lidocaine add much benefit in a Bier block?
questions.answer: No, it adds little or nothing

questions.stem: Why should long-acting local anaesthetics be avoided in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Risk of early cuff release

questions.stem: Why is mepivacaine less attractive for a Bier block?
questions.answer: It is a strong vasoconstrictor

questions.stem: How much local anaesthetic does a lower limb Bier block need?
How should the tourniquet be deflated in a Bier block?
questions.answer: In cycles

questions.stem: In a Bier block, after how long is the cuff first deflated and reinflated at once?
What early toxicity signs should be asked about after cuff deflation in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Tinnitus, light-headedness, metallic taste, signs of CNS excitation

questions.stem: In a Bier block, if no toxicity appears after about 1 minute, how long is the cuff reinflated?
In a Bier block, what is done with the cuff if toxicity is still absent after repeat deflation?
questions.answer: It can be released and removed

questions.stem: Why do brief cuff deflations reduce toxicity risk in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Each lets only a small part of the unbound drug into the circulation

questions.stem: Which serious complication follows tourniquet failure in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Systemic local anaesthetic toxicity

questions.stem: How often does leak under the cuff occur in upper limb Bier blocks?
What causes the very rare nerve injury in a Bier block?
questions.answer: Direct cuff pressure

questions.stem: What tourniquet time should be kept in a Bier block to limit tissue acidosis damage?
In which setting is compartment syndrome a rare complication of a Bier block?
questions.answer: Reduction of lower limb long-bone fractures
